entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded, socially/legally conferred relation that attaches to an agent (bearer) in virtue of their participation in a normative system. It is not internally grounded like a disposition, nor a quality. It is most naturally a Role (BFO_0000023): it inheres in a specific agent-bearer and is conferred by the legal or normative architecture external to that agent. The existing working:LegalObligation class (also subclass of BFO_0000023) is close, but 'agent-obligation binding' emphasizes the relational binding aspect — the specific nexus between a particular agent and an obligation — rather than the obligation type itself. A new class is warranted to capture this binding relation as a role-type SDC.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023) because it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in an agent-bearer and externally grounded in a normative or legal system.
AgentObligationBinding is a species of LegalObligation, specializing it to the specific binding of an obligation to a determinate agent-bearer, rather than the obligation type in general.

open_questions: Should AgentObligationBinding be a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation, or should it be a sibling class under BFO_0000023 that cross-cuts obligations and rights (i.e., any deontic binding to an agent)?

Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended to refer to the relational nexus (the specific token role inhering in one agent), or to a type of normative structure relating multiple agents (which might suggest a Disposition or even a GDC pattern)?
Is the bearer of an AgentObligationBinding always a human agent (BFO_0000040 material entity), or can it be an institutional/corporate agent as well?
Should this class be restricted to legal obligations, or does it generalize to moral or contractual obligations as well?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the specific nexus by which a normative obligation attaches to a determinate agent. In BFO 2020 terms, this is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent-bearer and is externally grounded — conferred by legal, contractual, or normative systems rather than arising from the intrinsic constitution of the agent. It is distinct from a Disposition (which is internally grounded) and from a Quality (which does not carry the normative-conferral structure). The existing working:LegalObligation class is also BFO_0000023 and captures obligation-types generally; AgentObligationBinding is proposed as a subclass that specializes to the token binding of such an obligation to a specific agent. The new class is proposed as a class (not an individual) because 'agent-obligation binding' names a kind, of which there can be many instances across different agents and legal systems.
